title: Ulyana and the Choir
premise: Tamsin Zhou has spent nine years hiding the gift of song-magic that once bound him to Veyra, a god who fell silent mid-prayer, leaving his mercenary choir dead and Tamsin hollow. When King Aldric declares a realm-wide hunt for the gifted, Tamsin is dragged back into the open by Ulyana, a fugitive girl whose voice can wake sleeping dragons—and who claims she hears Veyra still, screaming. Fleeing through Thornfell with a ragged found family of hunted singers, deserters, and one very old dragon, Tamsin learns the truth: the crown itself is a parasite, an ancient hunger wearing Aldric that devours gifted voices to stay alive. In the burning heart of the capital, Tamsin must choose between silencing his own voice forever—the price of survival he swore at Veyra's death—or singing the unbinding that will kill the thing on the throne, free the king, and let the last dragon's fire carry Veyra's final prayer home.
about_author: Beatrix Crane is the pen name of a former choir singer turned archivist who spent a decade cataloguing folk hymns in mountain villages before turning to fantasy. She writes about voices, vows, and the families we build in the margins of empires.

chapters.title: The Silent Tithe
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Smuggling salt through Thornfell, Tamsin pays a roadside shrine his wordless tithe to the silent god Veyra, revealing his grief and self-imposed muteness of magic. A crown patrol burns a village shrine nearby; he watches and does nothing. Emotional beat: guilt of the survivor who chose invisibility over intervention.

chapters.title: A Voice in the Snow
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. He finds Ulyana half-frozen in a smuggler's cave, hunted by crown wardens, her humming thawing the ice around them—song-magic he thought died with his choir. She says Veyra's name, and Tamsin's carefully buried gift stirs for the first time in nine years. Emotional beat: terror and longing colliding as the past knocks.

chapters.title: Wardens at the Waystation
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Crown wardens corner them at a mountain waystation; Ulyana's panicked song shatters their weapons, exposing them both. Tamsin kills for the first time since Veyra went silent and hates how easily it returns. Emotional beat: the hunt has begun, and hiding is officially over.

chapters.title: What the God Left Behind
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. In the ruins of Veyra's mountain chapel, Tamsin tells Ulyana how his choir died mid-hymn when the god fell silent, and why he swore off the gift. Ulyana insists she hears Veyra screaming beneath the world. Emotional beat: confession as release; grief shared is grief halved.

chapters.title: The Deserter's Road
chapters.summary: Brannic's POV. Brannic, a warden captain who tore off his own badge rather than burn children, joins them on the deserter's road, bringing news: the king's Edict of Ash lists names, and Tamsin's is first. Emotional beat: wary alliance; justice outside the law finds its first soldier.

chapters.title: Choir of Strays
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. In the free-town of Marrowgate they gather other hunted gifted: a mute drummer boy, twin harmonists, an old woman who sings storms. Tamsin resists leading again—he buried one choir already. Emotional beat: found family forming against his will, warmth threading fear.

chapters.title: Marrowgate Burns
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Wardens torch Marrowgate's gifted quarter. The strays escape through Tamsin's smuggler tunnels, but the old storm-singer stays behind to hold the gate and dies singing. Emotional beat: the price of survival made flesh; Tamsin's vow of neutrality shatters.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing the Crown
chapters.summary: Brannic's POV. Brannic reveals what he saw in the palace: King Aldric hasn't slept in six years, and something behind his eyes eats the captured gifted's voices. The Edict isn't policy—it's feeding. Emotional beat: horror reframes the hunt from cruelty to hunger.

chapters.title: Dragonfire Guttering
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. They reach the last dragon, Ysolde, ancient and dimming, chained by an old bargain to the crown. Ulyana's voice coaxes one ember of flame from her. Ysolde names the parasite: Hollowmoot, the god that ate gods. Emotional beat: awe and dread; the scale of the enemy revealed.

chapters.title: Veyra Screaming
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Deep beneath Thornfell, Ulyana leads Tamsin to where Veyra's silenced voice is imprisoned inside Hollowmoot. Through a shard of god-bone, Tamsin hears his god's unfinished prayer—and realizes finishing it is the unbinding. Emotional beat: hope with teeth; the mission gains its shape.

chapters.title: The Unbinding Rite
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The strays learn the rite requires many voices in true harmony—every singer risking everything, since Hollowmoot devours what it hears. Tamsin must sing lead, the role he held when his first choir died. Emotional beat: rehearsal as healing; choosing to lead again.

chapters.title: Bargain at the Border
chapters.summary: Brannic's POV. To reach the capital, Brannic bargains with his former warden brothers-in-arms, offering testimony against the crown in exchange for the army standing down. Some defect; some draw steel. Emotional beat: justice outside the law demands witnesses, not just blades.

chapters.title: Ashfall
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The company crosses the ash-choked lowlands where burned gifted villages smolder. The mute drummer boy, Pip, speaks his first words in years—to tell Tamsin he isn't his dead choir's ghost. Emotional beat: survivor's guilt confronted by a child's blunt grace.

chapters.title: The Gates of Verreholm
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Smuggler roads end at the capital's sewers. Inside, they find the palace dungeons full of caged voices, drained and murmuring. Ulyana nearly loses herself answering them. Emotional beat: dread deepening; the enemy's appetite made visible.

chapters.title: The King Who Remembers
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. In a forgotten corridor they meet Aldric himself—briefly lucid, the real king surfacing. He begs them to unbind him even if it kills him, and gives them the crown's one weakness: it cannot abide a finished prayer. Emotional beat: compassion for the monster's hostage.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Choir Loft
chapters.summary: Brannic's POV. One defected warden sells them out; wardens seize the twins and Pip. Brannic chooses to surrender himself in exchange, buying the others time and accepting likely death. Emotional beat: sacrifice as the found family's proof of itself.

chapters.title: The Devouring Throne
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Dragged before the throne, Ulyana watches Hollowmoot feed on the captives' voices, growing fat and radiant while Aldric drowns behind his own eyes. She begins to sing anyway, alone, buying seconds with pain. Emotional beat: defiance at the point of annihilation.

chapters.title: Every Voice We Have
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin, Ysolde, and the freed strays storm the throne hall. Ysolde's guttering fire breaks the dungeon cages; the drained captives' whispers join the choir. Tamsin takes the lead line and finally sings the prayer he abandoned nine years ago. Emotional beat: catharsis; grief transmuted into music.

chapters.title: The Last Note
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Climax. The unbinding rite tears Hollowmoot from Aldric, but it grabs Tamsin's voice in retaliation—as it took his choir. Ulyana and the choir finish the prayer without him, and Veyra's voice rises through dragon-fire to consume the parasite. Emotional beat: the price paid in full; survival redefined as what you give, not what you keep.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Ash and Song
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Hollowmoot dies; Aldric wakes, old and weeping, and abolishes the Edict. Tamsin survives but cannot speak above a whisper—his voice partly spent. The realm must now decide justice without a scapegoat: trials, not pyres. Emotional beat: exhausted dawn; victory that cost more than blood.

chapters.title: What Veyra Heard
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. On Veyra's rebuilt mountain, Tamsin buries his choir's names beside the finished prayer-stone. Veyra does not return—but the shrine answers with warmth, a god at rest rather than gone. Emotional beat: mourning completed; faith remade as gratitude instead of need.

chapters.title: The Choir That Remains
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Epilogue. The strays settle in Marrowgate's ruins and rebuild it as a sanctuary town where the gifted teach openly. Tamsin, whisper-voiced, conducts with his hands; Ulyana sings lead. Ysolde's ember brightens on the horizon. Emotional beat: found family enduring; the song continues in new throats.
